title: terraform: stabilize private GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking and state layout
author: Ethan Liu
description: Motivation: stabilize Terraform modules used by Private deployments to support GPU node pools, tightened IAM roles for least privilege, refined VPC networking defaults, and introduce a deterministic state layout/migration path. This PR consolidates several smaller fixes observed during on-prem pilot and addresses state drift found when migrating between clusters. Summary of changes: 1) gke_gpu_node_pool module: add explicit taints/tolerations, node auto-repair defaults, optional local-ssd and GPU type mapping, improved lifecycle rules to avoid node churn on label changes. 2) IAM: add custom roles for node bootstrap and private control-plane access, scope role bindings to service accounts in the private namespace, and add detailed policy docs. 3) Networking: default subnet CIDR calculations to avoid overlap with common corp ranges, expose optional secondary ranges for pod IPs, and add explicit route table tags for on-prem CNI integrations. 4) State layout: introduce modules/state backend v2 layout, migration helper scripts (migrate_state_v1_to_v2.sh) and terraform backend examples; document upgrade/rollback guidance for Private customers. Commit summary: squash commit combining feature branch work and follow-ups; earlier commits show iterative fixes for tests and CI. Changed files (high-level): modules/gke_gpu_node_pool/* (new variables, outputs, README), modules/iam/* (new custom_roles.tf, policy updates), modules/network/* (vpc defaults and docs), modules/state/* (backend config, migration script), examples/private/* (updated example cluster config), CI workflow tweaks to run new integration tests. Tests and CI: added unit tests for variable validation and two integration plans against the private example; initial CI run failed on linter errors and a flaky test for node pool autoscaling; addressed lints and added retries for integration plan; final CI status: all checks passing. Upgrade notes: provided a migration script and explicit step-by-step in modules/state/README.md. Checklist: - [x] Module unit tests added and passing - [x] Integration plan validated against example cluster - [x] Docs updated (module READMEs and example) - [x] Migration script and rollback notes included Related work: references ENG-4721 for on-prem pilot telemetry, INF-881 for state migration discussion, and SUP-204 for customer report that triggered the fix. Merge strategy: squash merge after approval. Release notes: see release_notes field below for end-user impact. Review conversation (high level): Priya: "Please scope the IAM role to the private namespace and document the escalation path." Author (Ethan): "Scoped role bindings, expanded README with escalation steps." Marisol: "Can we make the GPU type mapping extensible for future Ampere chips?" Author: "Added mapping table and example; left TODO for future GPUs with fallback behavior." Diego: "Node pool lifecycle changes look good; add integration test for label drift." Author: "Added a plan-based integration test that simulates label updates and verifies no recreate." QA notes: QA ran the migration script against a copy of the customer's state, verified terraform plan is a no-op post-migration. Security review: minimal privilege improvements to IAM; no new long-lived credentials added. Impact: customers using Private installer and Terraform modules should follow modules/state/README.md when upgrading; default behavior is backward compatible but state migration is required when moving to the new backend layout.

release_notes: Stabilize Private Terraform modules: GPU node pool improvements (taints/tolerations, SSD support, node lifecycle tuning), tighter IAM custom roles scoped to private namespace, safer VPC defaults and optional secondary ranges, and a documented state backend v2 with migration script. Note: operators must run the included migrate_state_v1_to_v2.sh and follow modules/state/README.md to upgrade without downtime. No breaking API changes to module inputs; some backend/state layout changes require migration.
